parts.label: (i)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Use the correct product rule - M1.

Obtain a correct derivative in any form, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-2e^{-2x}\ln(x-1)+\dfrac{e^{-2x}}{x-1}$ - A1.

Equate the derivative to zero and derive $x=1+e^{1/[2(x-1)]}$ or $p=1+e^{1/[2(p-1)]}$ - A1, AG.

Printed total: 3.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.answer: For the official printed expression $f(x)=\ln(x-1)-\dfrac1{2(x-1)}$, the scheme prints $f(2.2)=-0.234$ and $f(2.6)=0.317$, so a root lies between 2.2 and 2.6. Printed anomaly retained: the displayed expression actually gives $f(2.6)\approx0.1575$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Calculate values of a relevant expression or pair of relevant expressions at $x=2.2$ and $x=2.6$ - M1. For $f(x)=\ln(x-1)-\dfrac1{2(x-1)}$, $f(2.2)=-0.234$ and $f(2.6)=0.317$. Printed anomaly retained: the displayed expression actually gives $f(2.6)\approx0.1575$. Alternatively, the scheme prints $f(x)=+2e^{-2x}\ln(x-1)+\dfrac{e^{-2x}}{x-1}$, $f(2.2)=0.005\ldots$ and $f(2.6)=-0.0017\ldots$. Printed anomaly retained: the official line uses the plus sign before $2e^{-2x}\ln(x-1)$, inconsistent with its displayed values and with the derivative printed in part (i).

Complete the argument correctly with correct calculated values - A1.

Printed total: 2.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Use the iterative process $p_{n+1}=1+\exp\left(\dfrac1{2(p_n-1)}\right)$ correctly at least once - M1.

Obtain final answer $2.42$ - A1.

Show sufficient iterations to 4 d.p. to justify $2.42$ to 2 d.p., or show there is a sign change in the interval $(2.415,2.425)$ - A1.

Printed total: 3.
